barriers.reason: Patient reports the power was off twice this month for a day each time and is unsure refrigerated insulin stayed cold, so nightly insulin glargine storage is at risk.

alternatives.text: Complete the utility medical certification form to delay disconnection while refrigerated insulin is needed (limited duration; verify current rule).
Screen for LIHEAP utility assistance through CEDA/Cook County to help restore and maintain power; check current funding window.
Ask the pharmacy about insulin storage options or a lower-cost equivalent if refrigeration remains unreliable.

barriers.reason: A Tuesday 10:00 AM endocrinology visit conflicts with warehouse work 6 AM–2 PM and the patient loses hours with no sick days, so they may miss it again.

alternatives.text: Ask endocrinology for a later morning or evening appointment that does not conflict with the 6 AM–2 PM shift.
If the patient has another recurring medical trip, see if the endocrinology visit can be scheduled the same day/campus or via telehealth if no exam is needed.

barriers.reason: Thursday 2:00 PM class starts at the patient's shift end time (6 AM–2 PM), with no sick days, making weekly attendance difficult.

alternatives.text: Request a later class time or a different day that fits after the warehouse shift, or ask whether a make-up/online option exists.
See if the diabetes class can be paired with an existing medical visit day to reduce separate trips and time off work.
